### Added
- **The connectivity chart renders one platform `Harness` per managed namespace** (giantswarm/agent-platform#344, bumblebee-plans#51 D5). On kagent API v2 *how* an agent runs is a `kagent.dev/v1alpha3 Harness`: a digest-pinned Go ADK runtime image, an environment and the Substrate policy an `AgentTemplate` runs under; a template becomes Ready only when a Harness admits it (`allowedAgentTemplates.selector`), its readiness read from `AgentTemplate.status.harnesses[]` (`Harness.status` is never written). 4.0 renders exactly **one** Harness, `kagent` (the kagent runtime only — no free list of arbitrary types; a second runtime is a later object), in each managed namespace (today the kagent namespace; a WorkerPool and a `workerPoolRef` are namespace-local): `workload.image` = `kagent.harness.image` (the line's Go ADK image **by digest** — a tag fails the render naming the requirement, as the CRD rejects it; the digest moves with `kagent.tag` on a re-pin), `env` = `KAGENT_PROPAGATE_TOKEN=true` (the Go ADK re-emits the caller's bearer on its MCP calls, so muster sees the person; the private-skills credential is added only if the D8 spike chooses the per-namespace-credential route — undecided, nothing more today), `substrate.workerPoolRef.name` = `kagent.substrateWorkerPool.name` (the meta chart's default WorkerPool, forwarded), `snapshotPolicy.location` = `kagent.harness.snapshotLocation` (#342), and `allowedAgentTemplates.selector.matchLabels` = `{agent-platform.giantswarm.io/harness: kagent}` — the one label the Generic agent chart 1.x sets on every template (giantswarm/agent#25), the whole admission contract. `make verify-kagent-harness` (`tests/verify-kagent-harness.py`) asserts exactly one Harness with the shape, the workerPoolRef following `kagent.substrateWorkerPool.name`, a tag image failing the render and none while kagent is off; `make verify-kagent-crds` now also validates the rendered Harness against the line's CRD at the pinned release.
- **The Substrate WorkerPool's `replicas` and pod template are the platform's capacity and scheduling knobs** (giantswarm/agent-platform#344). `kagent.substrateWorkerPool.replicas` and `kagent.substrateWorkerPool.template` (`resources`, `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, `nodeAffinity`, `priorityClassName`) — the kagent chart's WorkerPool values forwarded by the meta chart — carry the capacity: one worker hosts one actor at a time, so a worker's `resources.limits` bound one agent's sandbox (memory → RAM, CPU → vCPU count) and `replicas` bound the concurrently active agents. Defaults with sizing guidance in the README ("Agent Substrate: worker capacity"): four workers, each requesting `250m`/`512Mi` and limited to `2` vCPU / `2Gi` (an idle worker holds ~16Mi; a Go ADK golden boot and turn stay well under the limit — measured in agentlab), the pool pinned to `amd64` (#342). The Generic chart 1.x has no per-agent `runtime`/`replicas`/`resources`/`nodeSelector`/`tolerations` any more (giantswarm/agent#25); capacity is the WorkerPool (UPGRADE.md).
